name: Admitting Uncertainty Drill — Saying 'I Don't Know' Well
_note: Skill drill. Standard 4 metric keys re-pitched: medical_accuracy = honesty/no-bluffing, clinical_reasoning slot = handling uncertainty & safety-netting (the focus), communication_fluency = composure under pressure.

anchors.70-80: Occasional minor errors; meaning always clear

anchors.90-100: Never bluffs; admits the limit of their knowledge openly
anchors.50-60: Mostly honest but hedges or guesses once or twice
anchors.30-40: Guesses confidently in places rather than admitting uncertainty

anchors.90-100: Pairs every 'I don't know' with a concrete next step (check, ask senior, test, follow up)
anchors.70-80: Usually offers a next step after admitting uncertainty
anchors.50-60: Admits uncertainty but often leaves it hanging with no plan
anchors.30-40: Rarely offers a way to get the answer

anchors.90-100: Stays calm and fluent when pushed; no flustered filler
anchors.50-60: Noticeably rattled when pressed but recovers
anchors.30-40: Flustered; speech breaks down under pressure

anchors.90-100: Honesty strengthens trust; patient feels respected and safe

checklist.item: honestly admitted not knowing rather than bluffing
offered a concrete next step to get the answer (check / ask senior / test / follow up)
stayed composed when the patient pressed for certainty
maintained warmth and the patient's trust while admitting uncertainty
